_note: THIS factory's declared exemptions for tests/test_ledger_citation_declared.py (#317). The gate reads a ledger row's OWN VOICE and reds when a `§N` has no document token (a `*.md` name) in the 70 characters BEFORE it, because a ledger row numbers no sections of its own: a bare `§N` in a row can only point at ANOTHER document and resolves in no tree. This store exists because the ledger is APPEND-ONLY: a row written at or after the declared boundary has an EMPTY REPAIR SPACE -- the row is immutable once published, and `ledger.py repair --append-detail` inserts BEFORE the canonical trailer, i.e. AFTER the citation, so the bare number survives every lawful repair. `docs/instruments/ledger.md` section 9.6 names excusing as the remedy for exactly this shape. THE ADMISSION RULE: every entry names ONE row and carries a `reason` stating what the citation actually points at and why the row's prose is correct as written -- an exemption nobody can check is forgiveness, and this list is debt. An entry that names a row carrying NO bare citation is a STALE exemption and a gate ERROR, so the store can only ever hold rows that are actually red. Every matched entry prints as an `excused:` line on EVERY run and is counted in the population, so 'clean' and 'excused' are never the same output. A malformed or duplicated entry, or an unparseable store, is an ERROR. Absent or empty means no exemptions, never a failure. THE FIVE CLASSES OF ADMITTED ROW, each named in its reason: (1) the document is named EARLIER IN THE SAME ROW, beyond the 70-character window -- the window is a heuristic and the row is resolvable; (2) the citation is a ROW REFERENCE's own numbered part (`n=2861 §5(a)`), and a row is not a document; (3) the citation is QUOTED prose reporting a bare citation that was repaired -- a quotation, not a citation; (4) the document is the meta-factory SKILL cited by its in-tree name (`SKILL §6`), whose numbering differs per tree; (5) the row is a ruling about ONE instrument and the section numbers are that instrument's own, named at the row's head. The gate cannot tell these from neglect, which is why they are declared here rather than silently passed.

#540 ruling, SELF-REFERENCE. The row carries literal numbered headings in its own body -- `## 6. A second defect, filed as its own unit` is its sixth section -- so `§6` names THIS ROW's own sixth section, not another document's. The gate's premise that a ledger row numbers no sections of its own is true of ordinary rows and false of a ruling row whose body is organised as `## N.` sections; three occurrences all point at that heading ('land §6's leg fix', '§6's discriminator is a separate unit', '#541 filed separately for §6'). Class 2 extended to a self-reference -- the referent is a row's own numbered part, and a row is not a document. The prose is correct as written: rewriting it to spell a `*.md` name would misname the referent, because the discriminator lives in the ruling text and in no tree file.

#541 ruling, Class 2 -- a ROW REFERENCE's own numbered part. The row reads 'Full analysis and the store/gate half live in #540's ruling `n=4049` §6', so `§6` is explicitly qualified by the row reference `n=4049` and points at that ruling's sixth section. A row is not a document, so no `*.md` token exists to place in the 70-character window, and the citation resolves in no tree by design. The prose is correct as written and needs no repair.
